activeForm: Giving the TAP layer Test::Builder's own STDOUT/STDERR dups
description:
FILED s521b (Opus, 2026-10-18) from #201 item 3, MEASURE FIRST (the s521b brief's member 3).  Pre-existing on main ed8a4504.

THE MEASUREMENTS (perl 5.40.3 vs PCL on the s521b tree, scratch/s521b/pr/cl1.pl):
  (a) close STDOUT; print "x"        perl: undef, continues     PCL: undef, continues   (SAME)
  (b) close STDOUT; open STDOUT, '>&', $saved     fileno 1 in both                         (SAME)
  (c) close STDOUT; open STDOUT, '>', $file       fileno 1 in both, the text lands          (SAME)
  (e) the same three for STDERR                   SAME (Capture-Tiny 07-stderr-closed now 872/0)
  (d) the TAP layer's OWN writes after the program closes STDOUT -- THE ONE MECHANISM:
      Capture-Tiny t/06-stdout-closed.t is `save_std(qw/stdout/); ok( close STDOUT, "closed STDOUT" );`
      perl: Test::Builder took its own dup of STDOUT at load (`open $Testout, ">&STDOUT"`), so `ok 1` goes
      to the ORIGINAL fd 1 through that dup and the file runs 872 rows.
      PCL: %tap-out (cl/pcl-test.lisp:16) writes to *standard-output* -- the program's CURRENT STDOUT --
      so `ok 1 - closed STDOUT` signals `#<fd-stream for "descriptor 1"> is closed` (an unhandled SBCL
      closed-stream-error, a Lisp backtrace; the END block dies the same way).  10-stdout-string.t is the
      same: `close STDOUT; open STDOUT, '>', \my $buf` -- perl's TAP still reaches fd 1, PCL's would go
      INTO the string (and dies first on the closed write).

WHY IT IS NOT FIXED IN s521b (needs a ruling): the fix is in the HARNESS, and the harness has TWO
personalities PCL serves with one writer.  perl's t/test.pl `_print`s to the CURRENT STDOUT (t/io/dup.t
reopens STDOUT and expects its `ok 8` to go through the reopen), while Test::More writes through dups
taken at load.  FIX SHAPE: `%test-import` (the `use Test::More` hook, cl/pcl-test.lisp ~295) dups fd 1
and fd 2 into TAP-private streams (autoflush on, as Test::Builder sets it); %tap-out and diag write there
when they exist; a test.pl file never calls %test-import and keeps today's behaviour.  Risks to measure:
the interleaving of a program's own STDOUT prints with TAP lines (two buffers on one fd -- Test::Builder
autoflushes its dups for exactly this), the fork/END paths, Pl/t rows that capture TAP + program output.
Harness change => the companion `--all --quick` PER BATCH (WHAT-TO-RUN table).  ACCEPTANCE: Capture-Tiny
06 + 10 one-file runs produce their 872 / 873 rows; their *FILE* rows leave baselines/cpan-board14-fails.tsv.


=== RULED (Fable, s521, 2026-10-18 17:0x; DECIDED ## s521) ===
The fix shape above IS the ruling: the TAP layer serving Test::More dups fd 1 and fd 2 in %test-import (autoflush on, Test::Builder's shape) and %tap-out / diag write there when they exist; perl-tests/t/test.pl's functions keep today's current-STDOUT behaviour (t/io/dup.t), told apart by the function called (the #3436 rule), never a global flag.  Harness change => the companion --all --quick per batch.  Scheduled: s521c member 2 (briefs-and-rules-for-claude-subagents/s521/s521c-prompt.md), together with #3434 part 2 (the no_plan trailer lost after restore_std), which is the same mechanism.


=== DONE (s521c, Opus 5.5, 2026-10-18, commit 7f73bd94) ===
%tap-open-stream (called from %test-module-imported, i.e. the first `use Test::More` / `Test::Simple`) dups descriptor 1 into *tap-stream* (the external format of that moment), autoflushed, and turns autoflush on for the program's STDOUT (Test::Builder's shape: a program line and a TAP line keep their order).  %tap-out writes to *tap-stream* when it exists, else the current STDOUT (test.pl's personality, t/io/dup.t).  Probes = perl byte for byte: close STDOUT then ok; re-open from a saved dup; the Capture-Tiny fileno spelling; STDOUT to an in-memory string; the no_plan trailer; a later binmode STDOUT ':utf8' does not reach the dup.  Guard Pl/t/tap-assert-01.t row 36, FAILS on 0b836815.  Capture-Tiny 06-stdout-closed 872/0, 10-stdout-string 873/0 (their *FILE* rows out); 13 / 14 / 23 print 1..873 / 1..873 / 1..877.
DEVIATION (for Fable): the failure diagnostics stay on the fd-1 dup instead of a dup of fd 2 -- tools/run-dist-t.pl reads TAP from stdout alone (#3241) and takes each failing row's got / expected from the lines after it; moving them would blank those columns on the board.  Test::Builder->output / failure_output / todo_output still answer the strings "STDOUT" / "STDERR", not the dup.
subject: Test::More's TAP must survive the PROGRAM closing STDOUT: PCL's TAP layer writes through the program's current *standard-output*, so `close STDOUT; ok(...)` dies with a raw SBCL closed-stream error (Capture-Tiny 06-stdout-closed + 10-stdout-string, 1,745 rows, #201 item 3)
